entities.summary:
Pope Eleutherius, also known as Eleutherus, was the bishop of Rome from c. 174 until his death in 189. His pontificate is alternatively dated to 171–185 or 177–193. He is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church.

Born into a Christian family, Eleutherius was educated in the classical traditions of Rome and became a priest during the reign of Emperor Marcus Aurelius. He was chosen as bishop of Rome at the age of 40 and faced numerous challenges, including the threat of persecution from the Roman Empire.

During his reign, Eleutherius played a key role in the development of the Catholic Church, establishing the office of the bishop of Rome and promoting the use of Latin in liturgical services. He also worked to strengthen the Church's connection to the broader Mediterranean world, establishing trade and diplomatic relations with neighboring states.

Eleutherius' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped to establish the foundations for the Catholic Church's enduring presence in Europe and beyond. He is remembered as a strong leader who worked tirelessly to promote the interests of the Church and its people.

Despite the passage of centuries, the impact of Pope Eleutherius' life and reign remains palpable, as the Catholic Church continues to draw on the traditions and teachings of its first centuries, including the importance of the bishop of Rome and the need for the Church to remain connected to the wider world.
